chapter: New York with Lester Young and Coleman Hawkins
title: Coleman Hawkins as a college of music
summary: Thompson calls Hawkins and Tatum ultimate teachers, discusses Hawkins' return from Europe and ranks him with Lester Young as tenor leaders.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: I'd like to -- perhaps we're digressing a little bit, but while we're speaking of Hawk I'd like to have you speak more about Hawk because he and Lester of course were the two greats, and of course were very different styles. Hawk too was a man that was -- had great depth as far as chord progressions and what not was concerned, harmonics and so on. Correct?
He was an adventurer, a musical adven-

turer, wasn't he? I refer to Coleman Hawkins as a college of music, jazz music, any kind of music, jazz music in particular. Because that's the way -- but you can remember that I've met people like Art Tatum, and I put Coleman Hawkins in the same category. These people were what you call the ultimate in teachers of music. If anyone had any kind of ear at all, had any kind of knowledge, and was interested at all in learning, you had to learn something from these people. And as I said, this was my primary reason for associating with these people as well as loving to listen to them I was intent on learning from them.

And as I said, Coleman Hawkins turned out to be a college of music for me, because he was involved in the highest form of progressions and music interpretation that there was around in those days. And he was considered to be one of the fathers of all times of this business (of) jazz music, you know. He had gone to Europe and on the strength of his ability he had created a reputation for himself that was incomparable. And he came back to the states in the midst of controversy about some of the young players like Don Byas or other players like Lester Young who they wanted to know whether he had lost his competitive spirit, or whether he had lost his inspiration, his ability to play. And he came back and proved it, that he was still one of the greats in the field of music. Although

like I said in my opinion I've always liked all of these musicians and I don't like to categorize musicians, but it's only natural that you compare them. And I always considered Lester Young and Coleman Hawkins to be the two leaders of the tenor saxophone playing, you know.
